metadata.note: Wrightsville and Tennille Railroad ('Wiggle and Twist'), Georgia: main line Tennille - Wrightsville - Dublin (36.3 mi), the former Oconee and Western Dublin - Dexter - Empire - Hawkinsville (38.8 mi) and the former Dublin and Southwestern Dublin - Rentz - Eastman (30.7 mi). Six features: the main line in three pieces drawn only in their own years - Tennille - Wrightsville 1885-1958, Wrightsville - Oconee east bank 1886-1958, and the Oconee River bridge into Dublin 1891-1958 (so the pre-bridge years do not claim the crossing, Rule 2); Dublin - Hawkinsville 1899-1907 [OPEN]; and Dublin - Eastman as two features with identical geometry split under Rule 4 at the July 1906 handover - Dublin and Southwestern 1905-1906, Wrightsville and Tennille 1906-1939 [OPEN]. Not drawn: the Dublin and Wrightsville's own 1885-1886 operation (folded into the W&T Wrightsville - east bank feature on the research report's recommendation - joint W&T/D&W schedule by Apr 1886, merger Dec 1886); the Empire and Dublin (1890-92) and Oconee and Western (1892-98) eras west of Dublin (no passenger timetable read - drawable NONE); the 1898 'Spring Haven Junction - End of Track' listing (unexplained, drawable NONE); and the Central of Georgia's Dover - Brewton - Dublin trains over W&T rails Brewton - Dublin (a CofG feature). The Central of Georgia financed the W&T from 1883 and owned it from 1899, but the W&T ran its own trains under its own name until passenger service ended - not a Rule 4 split; the 1971 merger into the CofG came after passengers ended. Colours #FC00C6 (Wrightsville and Tennille) and #FC0C00 (Dublin and Southwestern) are new to the dataset.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) MAIN LINE END: 1958 (15 Aug 1958, Georgia PSC) rests on one secondary source, a Dublin local historian; the last PRIMARY-confirmed year is 1951 (Aug 1951 mixed-train schedule in the Feb 1952 Official Guide). A PSC order or a Dublin Courier-Herald item of Aug 1958 would settle it. Applies to the Tennille - Wrightsville, Wrightsville - east bank and Oconee bridge features (their 1952-1958 segments). (2) [OPEN] Dublin - Hawkinsville: drawn to 1907, the last confirmed year (Mar 1907 Irwinton Bulletin timetable); the real end lies somewhere 1907-1941. The 1929 (and 1906) W&T timetables listed on railga.com have broken image links; recovering the 1929 one would likely move the end. (3) [OPEN] Dublin - Eastman (W&T): drawn to 1939 (Fowler 1939G); the last train left 28 Feb 1941, passenger status unknown. (4) Headways between the primary anchors (1886 double daily, 1907 two each way, 1951 one mixed round trip) are estimates; the four-daily peak and the post-1929 single round trip / 30 mph limit come from an unchecked local historian. (5) Oconee and Western / Empire and Dublin passenger service 1890-1898: RailGa lists 1894 and 1895 O&W timetables whose links are broken - recovering one would make that era drawable (at least an 1894 [ANCHOR]). (6) Spring Haven Junction - End of Track (MP 46-52, 1898 Guide): unexplained. (7) Location of the 1886-1891 Oconee River depot on the east bank, and whether the W&T's 1891 bridge stood on the site of the present (MD&S-tagged, 1901) bridge.
metadata.source_conflicts: Harrison - Wrightsville opening: ICC May 1885 vs Wikipedia (Atlanta Constitution) March 1885 - 1885 either way. D&SW opening: 1904 (local historian) vs 1905 (RailGa, Fowler 1905G, Jun 1906 paper) - drawn 1905. W&T takeover of the D&SW: Jul 1906 operating change (Wiregrass Farmer, local historian) vs 1907 formal acquisition (ICC, RailGa, Wikipedia) - split drawn at 1906. O&W purchase: 1896 (Wikipedia, RailGa) vs 1 Feb 1899 (ICC, local historian), W&T operation from Nov 1898 (Railroad Gazette) - drawn from 1899.

properties.geometry_quality: Tennille - Wrightsville: traced 16.4 mi against a documented 16.5 mi (Fowler/branchline.uk route 139 and the 1951 Official Guide; the ICC valuation gives 17.50 mi built including yard) - 0.6% short. 3.84 mi on OSM track tagged for the W&T, 12.56 mi on the OHM Atack line; NO straight-line (approximated) legs. That dataset is digitized from historical maps; measured against the W&T grades that ARE mapped in OSM west of Dublin, its sister ways lie a median 76-415 m and at most ~1.9 km off the true grade. Here it fits well: it meets the OSM Tennille track within 10-23 m, runs 20-210 m from Harrison's North/South Railroad Avenues, and every station milepost below lands within 0.3 mi of the Official Guide/Fowler figure. Station check, trace vs Fowler milepost from Tennille: Peacocks 5.8 vs 5.8, Harrison 9.3 vs 9.4, Donovan 13.3 vs 13.3, Wrightsville 16.4 vs 16.5. segments.note: Wrightsville and Tennille Railroad (chartered as the Wrightsville and Sun Hill 22 Dec 1883, renamed by charter amendment 28 Dec 1883 when the terminus moved from Sun Hill to Tennille), Tennille - Peacocks (5.8) - Harrison (9.4) - Donovan (13.3) - Wrightsville (16.5), steam from opening. Tennille - Harrison opened 24 Dec 1884 (ICC valuation); Harrison - Wrightsville in 1885 (ICC: May 1885; Wikipedia, citing the Atlanta Constitution of 24 May 1885: completed March 1885 - conflict recorded, either way 1885). Wrightsville Recorder 17 Jan 1885: 'We have daily trains running within a mile and a half of Wrightsville'; an excursion train reached Wrightsville by 28 Mar 1885; fares posted Feb 1885 at 4 cents a mile; 1,700+ ticketed passengers in May 1885. Drawn from 1885, the first full year: the last week of 1884 to Harrison is omitted. Tennille was a union station for the Central of Georgia, Sandersville Railroad, Augusta Southern and W&T; shops at Tennille until a 1923 fire, rebuilt at Dublin 1924. The Central of Georgia financed the W&T from the start and owned it from 1899, but the W&T ran its own trains under its own name (1899-1907 newspaper cards, 1951 Guide table) - a stock relationship, not a Rule 4 split. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE: the Dublin Post of 28 Apr 1886 advertised double daily trains from 1 May 1886 (primary); a local historian's 'four daily passenger trains' at the peak is unchecked; no year-by-year count was read. The 1929 boundary is the same local historian's 'one round trip a day after 1929' (unchecked).
sources: Segment-level: start from the ICC valuation opening dates and the Wrightsville Recorder 17 Jan and 28 Mar 1885 items (gahistoricnewspapers.galileo.usg.edu, lccn sn90052204); 1886 frequency from the Dublin Post 28 Apr 1886 p3 (lccn sn90052270); 1929 boundary from the local historian (unchecked) - as read in research/branches/wrightsville_and_tennille_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these sources.

segments.note: Built by the Dublin and Wrightsville Railroad (the Central of Georgia paid half its cost): Wrightsville - Meadows (21.5) - Lovett (23.8) - Manning [Donaldson] (25.5) - Brewton [Bruton] (27.9) - Condor (32.3) - Oconee River depot on the east bank opposite Dublin (mileposts from Tennille). Trains reached Lovett by Oct 1885 (local historian, no paper cited) and Condor in May 1886 (Wrightsville Recorder 29 Apr 1886: 'The W. & D. train will run thro' to Condor next Saturday'); the Dublin Post of 28 Apr 1886 advertised a joint 'schedule of the W. & T. and D. & W. railroad', double daily trains from 1 May 1886; first passenger train at the Oconee River depot 8 Sep 1886; the D&W merged into the W&T in Dec 1886. Drawn as W&T from 1886: the D&W's separate operation (1885 - Dec 1886) is NOT split out as its own feature, on the research report's recommendation - through running on a joint W&T/D&W schedule was in place by Apr 1886 and the D&W's only dated passenger evidence is 1886; the partial 1885 service to Lovett is not drawn. Before the 1891 bridge, Dublin passengers and freight crossed the Oconee by ferry and wagon - this feature stops at the east bank. Brewton - Dublin was also used by the Central of Georgia's own Dover - Brewton - Dublin trains (c.1900 on), which belong to the CofG layer, not this one. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE anchored on the 1886 double-daily schedule (primary); the four-daily peak is a local historian's unchecked statement. The 1929 boundary is the local historian's 'one round trip a day after 1929' (unchecked).
sources: Segment-level: start from the Wrightsville Recorder 29 Apr 1886 p3 and Dublin Post 28 Apr 1886 p3 (gahistoricnewspapers.galileo.usg.edu) and the 8 Sep 1886 first train to the river (local historian); D&W merger Dec 1886 per the ICC valuation and the local historian; 1929 boundary unchecked - as read in research/branches/wrightsville_and_tennille_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these sources.

segments.note: Wrightsville and Tennille operation of the former Oconee and Western (ex Empire and Dublin, built 1889-90 from an Empire Lumber Co. logging road): Dublin - South Western Junction - Hutchings [Harlow] - Vincent - Springhaven - Dexter - Alcorns - Chester - Yonkers - Roddy - Empire - Bailey's Park [Sparrows] - Cypress - Hawkinsville (also 'Luckie' in 1899). The Railroad Gazette of 18 Nov 1898 says the O&W 'will henceforth be operated in connection with the Wrightsville & Tennille'; formal purchase 1 Feb 1899 (ICC; other sources say 1896 - conflict recorded). The Record 16 Mar 1899 prints a W&T timetable through Dexter, Alcorns, Chester, Yonkers, Empire and Luckie to Hawkinsville; further cards in The Record 8 Mar 1900, Sandersville Herald 1904-05 ads, an excursion Tennille - Hawkinsville - Fitzgerald 31 Jul 1905, and the Irwinton Bulletin 8 Mar 1907 with two trains each way (e.g. Dexter 9:20 - Empire 10:00 - Hawkinsville 10:27 AM). [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1907 by that Mar 1907 timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped; it very likely ran on, possibly into the late 1930s, and the line was abandoned in 1941 (an abandonment date, NOT a passenger end). Do not extend without evidence: a 1929 W&T timetable listed on railga.com (broken image link) is the most likely next proof. A 1918 government war-relic exhibit train Hawkinsville - Tennille is an exhibit special and is not counted. The Oconee and Western (1892-1898) and Empire and Dublin (1890-1892) eras are NOT drawn: no timetable for either was read. Headway 720 min reflects the two trains each way of the 1899 and 1907 cards; intermediate years are an estimate.

segments.note: Dublin and Southwestern Railroad (chartered 1904, president E. P. Rentz, built entirely with local capital): Dublin - South Western Junction (2.3) - Garretta [Tingle] (7.3) - Rentz (12.7) - Mullis (16) - Cadwell (17.1) - Batson [Della] (19.6) - Leon [Colemans] (21.7) - Plainfield [Beehive] (22.6) - Sutherland (25.5) - Eastman (30.7), connecting with the Southern Railway at Eastman. In the 1905 Official Guide (Fowler route 140 tags Dublin, Rentz, Eastman etc. '1905G'); RailGa: completed to Eastman in mid-1905; Wiregrass Farmer 29 Jun 1906: 'has been in operation for one year'. A local historian says it began operating in 1904 - conflict recorded; 1905 is the proven year. Operation passed to the Wrightsville and Tennille c. 1 Jul 1906 (Wiregrass Farmer 29 Jun 1906: 'after next Sunday the road will be operated as a part of that system'); the ICC valuation and RailGa give 1907, the formal deed / charter amendment (8 Aug 1907) - conflict recorded, split drawn at the 1906 operating change. 1906 is drawn in both this feature and the W&T Dublin - Eastman feature because the handover fell mid-year. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE (two trains each way appear on the W&T's Mar 1907 card for this line; no D&SW-era count was read).

segments.note: Wrightsville and Tennille operation of the former Dublin and Southwestern, from c. 1 Jul 1906 (Wiregrass Farmer 29 Jun 1906; ICC and RailGa give the formal 1907 acquisition - conflict recorded). The W&T's Mar 1907 advertisement (Irwinton Bulletin 8 Mar 1907) still headed this table 'DUBLIN & SOUTHWESTERN R. R.' - the W&T kept the name for the division in its card - with two trains each way. Fowler tags every station on the branch 'bc' or 'abc', i.e. in the 1926 and 1939 Official Guides. [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1939 by the 1939 Guide listing. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. The ICC authorized abandonment c. Oct 1940 (finding 'little public need'), and the last train left Dublin on 28 Feb 1941 (local historian) - whether that train carried passengers is not established. Do not extend without evidence. A Service Coach Lines bus Eastman - Dublin - Wrightsville advertised in Dec 1935 is a bus table and says nothing about the trains either way. Headway 720 min is the 1907 two-each-way figure carried forward - an ESTIMATE for later years.
